newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Hollinger sweetens bid for Southam majority.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Hollinger sweetens bid for Southam majority.

text.p: International publisher Hollinger Inc. has sweetened its offer to buy just enough shares in Southam Inc. to give it a majority stake in Canada's largest newspaper publisher.
Hollinger, which now holds 41 percent of Southam, on Wednesday raised its offer to C$20 ($15) per share, or C$140 million ($105 million) in all, for 7 million shares of the company.
The Canadian publisher's original offer was C$18.75 ($14.05) per share, worth about C$131 million ($98 million).
Hollinger said an independent committee of Southam directors intended to recommend the offer to Southam shareholders.

"The special committee ... considering the offer has been advised by RBC Dominion Securities Inc. that the C$20-per-share price is fair from a financial point of view and the special committee intends to recommend that Southam shareholders accept the offer," Hollinger said in a statement.
The bid would raise Hollinger's stake to 50.1 percent of Southam, which owns 20 dailies, including the Montreal Gazette, the Ottawa Citizen and the Vancouver Sun.

Canadian-born press baron Conrad Black's Hollinger and Hollinger International Inc. own or have interests in the London Daily Telegraph, the Chicago Sun-Times, the Jerusalem Post and the Sydney Morning Herald.
In May, he boosted his stake in Southam to 41 percent from below 20 percent by buying Power Corp. of Canada's 16.4 million Southam shares.
Black prefers to own more than 50 percent of those assets he buys so he can consolidate their earnings on the balance sheets of his holding companies.
At the Southam committee's request, Hollinger agreed to revise its right to buy more shares under the offer.
Hollinger agreed not to acquire more than 8.5 million Southam shares unless it met certain requirements, including telling Southam shareholders exactly how many shares it is willing to acquire.

Hollinger also agreed that shareholders would have 10 days to deposit their shares after receiving notice of a change to the offer. Southam shareholders would also have the right to withdraw shares deposited during that 10-day period.
Hollinger said a notice of variation regarding the sweetened offer would be mailed to Southam shareholders on or around Friday.
